- **PSS 4421 - Principles of Weed Science:** Fundamentals of chemical weed control, herbicide families, usage, and application methods.
- **PSS 3323 - Crop Physiology:** Concepts underlying crop physiology, including phenology, canopy development, photosynthesis, and dry matter partitioning.

- Graduates are prepared for roles in agriculture, horticulture, crop production, environmental consulting, vineyard management, and more.

Glossary

$10K Degree Completion Program. Texas Tech's pathway for adults who already have college credit and want to finish a bachelor's degree. "10K" means a target cost of about $10,000 for students who qualify. It is not a financial filing. You may also see it written as 10K or 10-K. Two degrees are available: a Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies and a Bachelor of Science in Leadership Studies. If you qualify, you could finish for as little as $10,000. Your advisor will estimate your cost, because it depends on the credit you already have.

Applicable credit hours. College credit that counts toward this degree, not every credit you have earned. With at least 80 applicable credit hours, including your core courses, you could finish for as little as $10,000. With 70 to 79, you can still enroll. Your advisor will tell you which of your credits apply.

Core curriculum (core courses). The general-education courses you need before you can finish a bachelor's degree. This program expects those courses to be complete before you start.

Asynchronous. Coursework you complete on your own schedule. It is not a live class at a set time. After the microcredentials, the rest of the degree is taught this way.

Hybrid. A mix of online work and in-person class. In this program, the microcredentials are online, with in-person meetings two Saturdays a month at Texas Tech DFW or Texas Tech El Paso. You can choose a morning session (9 AM–12 PM) or an afternoon session (1 PM–4 PM).

Microcredential. A free 4-week course led by Texas Tech faculty. This program has four required courses. You can take them in any order, and textbooks are included. If you complete them, you can turn them into 12 credit hours toward your degree. Each course also comes with a digital badge.

Digital badge. An online record that shows you finished a microcredential. You earn one for each course.

**Course Structure for TTU Online Graduate Programs**

- **8-Week Terms:**  
  Graduate courses are delivered in accelerated 8-week terms instead of traditional 16-week semesters. This allows you to focus on fewer courses at a time and progress efficiently toward your degree.

- **100% Online & Asynchronous:**  
  All courses are fully online and asynchronous, meaning there are no required live class meetings. You can complete coursework on your own schedule each week.

- **Multiple Start Dates:**  
  The 8-week model provides multiple start dates throughout the academic year, offering flexibility for when you begin or continue your coursework.

- **Enrollment Status:**  
  - Full-time: 6 credit hours per 8-week term
  - Half-time: 3–5 credit hours per 8-week term
  - Less than half-time: 1–2 credit hours per 8-week term
  Most students take 1–2 courses per term, depending on their goals and schedule.

- **Workload Expectation:**  
  Students should plan for approximately 90 minutes of study daily per course.

- **Course Design:**  
  Courses are structured with weekly assignments and deadlines to keep you on track, but you have the flexibility to complete work at times that fit your life.

**Support & Flexibility**
- Designed for working professionals and those balancing family or other commitments.
- Access to academic advising, student advocates, tutoring, writing center support, and technical support.

Texas Tech University offers a fully online Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences (BAAS) in Applied Leadership, designed for working adults, military personnel, and transfer students who want to complete their education and advance their careers.

- **Format:** 100% Online – Asynchronous
- **Ideal For:** Students with an Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree from an accredited institution.
